html: I. שׁוּק (√ of foll., meaning dub.; Arabic سَاقَ is drive beast, etc., carry on affairs; Ethiopic ሶቀ: sustain; cf. Arabic سَاقٌ leg, especially shank, Aramaic שׁוֹקָא leg (rare), ܫܳܩܳܐ leg, thigh; connexion dub. with Assyrian sûḳu, street, Aramaic שׁוּקָא, ܫܽܘܩܳܐ, street, market-place (whence Arabic سُوقٌ loan-word according to Frä 187; but then س = שׁ?), Palm. שוק id., Lzb 373).
